chunks: 4824 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who abandons his wife without divorce and without an oath for a year, and does not come to her bed. He said: “Let him go to his wife.”

And he عليه السلام said: “Any man who makes īlāʾ regarding his wife—and īlāʾ is that he says, ‘By Allah, I will not have relations with you for such and such,’ or, ‘By Allah, I will surely anger you,’ then he continues to anger her—then he is to be given a waiting period of four months. Then after the four months, he is brought and made to stand. If he returns, that is, that he reconciles with his wife…”

And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce. No divorce takes place between them until he is made to stand, and if it is also after the four months, then he is compelled either to return or to divorce.”

And it is narrated: “If he returns, meaning that he goes back to intercourse; otherwise, he is imprisoned in an enclosure of reeds, and hardship is imposed upon him in food and drink until he divorces.”
And it has been narrated: “Whenever the Imam of the Muslims commands him to divorce and he refuses, his neck is struck because of his refusal against the Imam of the Muslims.”

key_terms.إِمَامُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The authority of the Muslims who enforces legal rulings.
key_terms.الطَّلَاقِ: Divorce, the formal dissolution of marriage.
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءُ: A husband's oath to abstain from marital relations with his wife.
key_terms.فَاءَ: He returned, meaning he resumed proper marital relations or reconciliation.
key_terms.يَهْجُرُ: He abandons or keeps away from his wife.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband who swears to abstain from his wife or abandons her without divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling of īlāʾ, when a husband swears to abstain from marital relations with his wife, and distinguishes it from mere abandonment without oath. It establishes a four-month period after which he must either return to conjugal life or be compelled to divorce, with enforcement carried out through judicial authority. The report highlights both spousal rights and the role of the Imam or ruler in enforcing family law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4824 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who abandons his wife without divorcing her or taking an oath, leaving her for a year without approaching her bed.
Imam (as) said: "He must return to his wife."

Imam (as) also said: "Any man who swears an oath (ilaʾ) against his wife-ilaʾ being when he says, 'By Allah (swt), I will not have relations with you for such and such time' or 'By Allah (swt), I will anger you,' and then he continues to upset her, he is to be given four months.
After those four months, he will be brought forward. If he reconciles with his wife, which means returning to her, then

But if he does not reconcile, he will be forced to divorce her. However, no divorce will occur between them until he is brought forward, and even after the four months, he will be compelled either to reconcile or to divorce."

It is also narrated: "If he reconciles, meaning he returns to marital relations, then so be it. Otherwise, he will be imprisoned in a pen made of reeds and will be subjected to hardship in food and drink until he divorces her."

Additionally, it is narrated: "Whenever the Imam of the Muslims commands him to divorce and he refuses, his neck shall be struck (execution) due to his defiance against the authority of the Imam of the Muslims."
